Jailbreak.d: An input designed to get an AI model to ignore its safety training and produce content it would normally refuse. A form of prompt injection aimed at the model's own rules.

Lethal trifecta.d: Simon Willison's name for the risky combination of an AI agent having access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and a way to send data out. Together they allow prompt injection to steal data.

PII.d: Personally identifiable information: any information that identifies a person directly (name, email, phone, PAN, Aadhaar number) or indirectly when combined with other data.

Pseudonymisation.d: Replacing identifying values with consistent stand-ins (such as customer_17) while keeping a separate key that can reverse it. Under GDPR, pseudonymised data is still personal data.

Data loss prevention.d: DLP: tools and rules that detect sensitive data, such as card numbers or secrets, and warn or block when it is about to leave approved places.

Data residency.d: Control over which country or region data is processed and stored in, often required by law, contracts or company policy.

EU AI Act.d: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the European Union's law regulating AI systems by risk tier (prohibited, high-risk, transparency, minimal) plus rules for general-purpose AI models. It applies in stages from 2025 to 2028.

High-risk AI system.d: Under the EU AI Act, an AI system used in a sensitive area such as recruitment, credit scoring or education (Annex III), or as a safety component of a regulated product (Annex I). It must meet strict testing, documentation, logging and oversight requirements.

General-purpose AI model.d: Under the EU AI Act, a model trained on broad data that can perform many different tasks, such as a large language model. Its providers have documentation and copyright duties, with extra duties for models with systemic risk.

GDPR.d: The EU's General Data Protection Regulation (2016/679), in force since May 2018. It governs how personal data of people in the EU is processed, including by organisations outside the EU.

Data protection impact assessment.d: DPIA: a documented assessment of the risks a data-processing activity poses to people and how they will be reduced. Required by GDPR for high-risk processing and yearly for Significant Data Fiduciaries under India's DPDP Rules.

DPDP Act.d: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which governs digital personal data, made operational by the DPDP Rules, 2025, with core duties phased in over eighteen months.

Data Fiduciary.d: Under India's DPDP Act, the organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed (similar to a 'controller' under GDPR).

NIST AI RMF.d: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology's voluntary AI Risk Management Framework (2023), organised into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.

ISO/IEC 42001.d: The international standard (2023) for an AI management system: the policies, roles, risk processes and controls an organisation uses to manage AI. It can be certified by an accredited auditor.
